races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash (Class 2 Handicap)

runners_data.name: Kendall Roy
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D on good ground in recent form (3rd, 1st, 9th in last three runs), trainer McGivern firing at 1/2 over 14 days, prominent racer who should secure a clean position just off the lead; recent sim-going record is strong (3W) and the 142lb weight is the main concern.
runners_data.comment: Kendall Roy shaped well when third last time out, and a winner three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour at a competitive 142 lb; the risk is that two unplaced efforts in his recent record hint at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Tuco Salamanca
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who will be ridden from off the pace by Jerry Chau, best form comes over 6f on standard/good ground and the drop to 5f on faster footing is a slight query; Sangster yard showing good recent form (4/15 T14) but the slower pace profile makes this hard to fancy in a likely-honest gallop.
runners_data.comment: Tuco Salamanca arrives on the back of an unplaced effort seven days ago, though he was a winner two starts back, and his rating of 100 leaves him mid-pack among these rivals; experience over today's trip and going helps, but that sixth three starts back suggests some inconsistency to overcome.

runners_data.name: Fahrenheit Seven
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two recent wins over 5f on standard ground for Cowell, but the trainer is 0/13 in the 14-day window and 42 days off the track adds a fitness caveat; the headgear (hood) is retained and the sim-going record of 3W is solid, but the absence from the track is a flag.
runners_data.comment: Fahrenheit Seven has run over today's trip and shown he can win, with back-to-back victories four and five starts back; however, two consecutive unplaced efforts in recent starts are a concern, and 42 days off adds a fitness query at 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Fandom
runners_data.note: Hannon runner who has been busy (7d since last run) and handles this ground well (11/13 sim-going, 1W4P); prominent style suits the likely shape but finishing positions have been creeping back (24th, 3rd, 4th, 13th in recent pattern) and the 6f form dominates his history.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to claim third two starts back after a below-par effort, and he has experience of today's distance and going — Fandom arrives fit on a seven-day turnaround and our rating of 104 marks him as a genuine threat; the risk is that last-time-out unplaced run needs forgetting quickly.

runners_data.name: Spartan Arrow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Moore and Watson but 99 days off the track is a serious concern — last five runs all returned placed-to-well-beaten finishes on going variants he handles; the blinkers are retained and Ascot sim-going record (8/15) is moderate, making this tough to enthuse about at the weights.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 99 days off, Spartan Arrow nevertheless carries a rating of 106 from stall five and has experience of today's trip and conditions — the concern is whether this string of unplaced efforts signals a horse out of form.

runners_data.name: All Ways Glamorous
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 5f on good ground in recent outings (1st, 1st in hist), the strongest piece of form in this field; Mason yard is active (2/8 T14) and the mare's sim-going record of 4W7P is the best in the race, making her the standout fit for the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and again last time out, so All Ways Glamorous arrives in form, but he ranks last on our figures and that six-point gap to his official rating makes him hard to fancy at the weights despite the distance and going experience.

runners_data.name: Gaeli
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who wears blinkers and needs things to fall right from the back; last sim-going run on good ground finished 1st but that is one from six in those conditions and recent form reads 1-6-5-6-0 — the Kirby yard is 0/13 over 14 days, compounding the concern.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last four starts, Gaeli at least has experience over today's trip and a win in his recent form to draw on, but that sequence of unplaced and minor finishes is hard to ignore; 43 days off and 136 lb make this a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Gold Star Hero
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Bell, with three consecutive wins before a blank last time; all best form came on standard or soft ground (sim-going on good 0/0 wins) which is a notable caveat on today's quick surface, and the hood is retained; will set the early tempo but may find the ground quicker than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out and ranked 11th of 12 on our figures, Gold Star Hero faces a stiff task despite three wins in his last five starts; a struggling trainer at 4% in the last 14 days only adds to the concern, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Bolo Neighs
runners_data.note: Beckett runner (6/50 T14) with good Ascot course knowledge and a recent win over 6f on good; naturally wants to race prominently but this field's pace congestion means he is very likely to be shuffled back from his preferred berth — his chance is real if he can find a run, but the style compromise tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in four of his last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Bolo Neighs makes for a tough sell, though he has distance and going experience to call on and a third two starts back offers a flicker of hope.

runners_data.name: Cinque Verde
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner for Carroll, carrying race-day experience (11d LR) and a course win in recent form; sim-going record (2W) is moderate on good ground and all five recent runs came over 6f, so the drop to 5f combined with a contested lead battle is a double query.
runners_data.comment: Cinque Verde has struggled for consistency, finishing unplaced and eighth in her last two starts, and she ranks tenth of twelve on our figures. The win three starts back offers a flicker of hope, and she has run over today's distance and going before, but little else invites confidence here.

runners_data.name: Apollo One
runners_data.note: Veteran (8yo) prominent racer whose recent form shows a string of mid-to-back-of-field finishes on good ground (10th, 14th, 9th, 3rd, 9th in hist); the Charalambous/Clutterbuck yard is 0/5 over 14 days and he shares the redistribution issue with Bolo Neighs — racing out of his natural position makes his chance slim.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Apollo One nonetheless shaped with promise when third four starts back and runner-up six starts back, and he arrives here fit on a 14-day turnaround with experience of today's distance and going — our rating of 108 marks him out as the one to beat from stall 12 off 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Cowell's second string, wears a visor and is a genuine hold-up type whose recent figures are poor across the board (12th, 6th, 8th, 15th, 7th in hist); the yard is 0/13 in the T14 window and no jockey listed in the data — this requires a dramatic collapse of the pace scenario to factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Kylian heads here off a 14-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and conditions in his favour, but a string of unplaced efforts gives little cause for confidence; 130 lb from stall ten makes his task no easier.

races.paceDynamic: Gold Star Hero and Cinque Verde are confirmed front-runners who will battle for the early lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested gallop over Ascot's straight 5f on good-to-firm ground. Five of the twelve runners want prominent positions — Kendall Roy, Fahrenheit Seven, Fandom, Spartan Arrow, and All Ways Glamorous will all be hunting the space just behind the leaders, creating a compressed and potentially messy early phase between the 2f and 3f marks where crowding is a real risk. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly: Bolo Neighs and Apollo One are both natural prominent racers who have been pushed back in the map, with Gold Star Hero, Cinque Verde, and All Ways Glamorous best-placed to actually secure their preferred early positions given recent form and draw. An honest, competitive gallop on quick ground over 5f at Ascot is a course-and-distance stamping ground that typically rewards horses who can sit close to a genuine pace and sustain their effort through the final furlong — the prominent-to-midfield horse with clean air and a strong finishing stride is the profile this shape serves best, rather than the true front-runners who will likely have burned each other out, or hold-up horses who will have too much ground to find from off a fast pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Run Down Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Gold Star Hero and Cinque Verde cut each other up early, a horse sitting second or third can cruise into contention and sustain the effort to the line.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners trade blows from the start, burning their reserves by the 2f pole and leaving the perfect target for a prominent racer to pounce; Ascot's 5f favours those who travel comfortably in the first half and quicken in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates From Flag
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed front-runners — most likely Gold Star Hero — establishes a clear lead early and sets a controlled rather than frenetic gallop.
scenarios.body: With Cinque Verde likely to push on from the outside and Gold Star Hero asserting dominance, whichever of the two gets first run on the rail can dictate margins and hold on if rivals cannot quicken past on ground that rewards early momentum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly strong and creates a gap for horses sitting in fifth or sixth to find a clear run and cut through a tiring field in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Bolo Neighs, despite being pushed back from its natural prominent position, retains good Ascot form and the ability to find a split late; Kylian and Gaeli are genuine hold-up types who could benefit if the fractions are truly searching but their recent figures make this a stretch.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace absolutely collapses over the final furlong and every prominent type fades simultaneously, opening the door for the two genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Tuco Salamanca has course and distance experience and the jockey to deliver late, but this scenario requires an unusually strong collapse of a field that contains several resolute finishers; Kylian's headgear (visor) and poor recent figures make this a low-confidence shape.

watchPoints.text: All Ways Glamorous — back-to-back 5f wins on good ground with the best sim-going strike rate in the field; if Mme Velon secures a clean berth just off the leaders, she is the most dangerous prominent runner in the race.

Gold Star Hero and Cinque Verde — watch the battle for the early lead in the first furlong; if one or both burn each other out hard in the first 2f, the race opens dramatically for the prominent midfield pack and the leader may stop quickly inside the final furlong.

Kendall Roy — trainer on a sharp 1/2 T14 strike rate and the horse won this course and distance last time out; the prominent draw position could be compromised by the traffic congestion at the 2-3f mark, making a clean run essential.

Bolo Neighs and Apollo One — both natural prominent types who will likely be shuffled back by the pace volume; watch in running for them finding room, but a style compromise this significant over only 5f rarely resolves in their favour.

Spartan Arrow (99d absence) and Fahrenheit Seven (42d) — two prominent runners returning from notable breaks; if either shows signs of race-rustiness early they become a traffic hazard for horses trying to secure a clean run through the pack.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers (Class 2 Handicap) (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Spirit Mixer
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner at OR 94, eight-year-old who has won and placed over this exact trip on soft and Good; Saffie Osborne takes over and Andrew Balding's yard is in solid 14-day form — the horse gets its preferred role and must be respected as a genuine pace-control factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Spirit Mixer nonetheless catches the eye with a third and a fourth in recent form, has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 100 suggests he's better than his mark; the risk is he's been off 42 days and may need the run.

runners_data.name: Lavender Hill Mob
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a win over 21f on soft ground and an OR of 92; the best recent form came on softer surfaces (SOF wins) so the Good to Firm description here is worth monitoring, and 53 days off adds a mild fitness query despite the headgear (p).
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Lavender Hill Mob at least posted a third four starts back, though recent efforts have been disappointing; he has run over today's distance and going before, and at 134 lb faces a stiff task off a 53-day absence.

runners_data.name: Kilmeaden
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent racer from a yard hitting 1-from-10 in the 14-day window, with form figures of 3 and 5 on Good and Soft; the headgear (t) is unchanged and the trip is 2f further than the horse's best handicap mark was earned — stamina over 2m needs proving.
runners_data.comment: Kilmeaden shaped with plenty of promise when third two starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; winless in his last five starts, though, is the concern.

runners_data.name: Dancing In Paris
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form reads poorly (9th and 15th in last two) and whose Good-ground record shows only a single placed effort in nine tries at similar trips; Ian Williams runs three in this race and this looks the least interesting of the trio on current form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dancing In Paris nevertheless shaped with promise when fifth last time out, and returning after just 15 days he arrives fit and with experience of today's distance and going — his 132 lb burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Shrimp Shady
runners_data.note: Progressive four-year-old with three wins from five starts, including two on Good and one on Good to Firm at distances of 1m4f–1m6f; Ryan Moore takes the ride for Balding and the horse's ability to sit prominently and quicken makes it the natural beneficiary of a steady-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Shrimp Shady won last time out and has a lively recent record — a winner three starts back and fifth starts back too — but ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, he faces a stiff ask under 132 lb, making him hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Mountain Road
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer who has won and finished placed on Good ground at 1m3f–1m6f, but the step up to 2 miles is a question at OR 87; Yutaka Take adds international intrigue, and 69 days off the track is the longest absence in the field.
runners_data.comment: Mountain Road won last time out but has been off 69 days, his trainer is in poor form at 2/40 over the past fortnight, and carrying 129 lb adds another burden; he has run over today's trip and going before, though, giving him something to build on.

runners_data.name: Marnier
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in terms of natural style, though the map places it in midfield due to field congestion — its four-year-old profile and OR 87 on Good ground is solid, with a win over 1m2f and places at 1m1f suggesting stamina at 2m is unproven; the style displacement is the key concern.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Marnier is hard to fancy despite a win last time out; that recent victory is the obvious plus, but his overall recent form is inconsistent and the speed rating of 82 leaves him well short of the standard required here.

runners_data.name: Oneforthegutter
runners_data.note: Another true hold-up type repositioned to midfield by the map — form figures of 8,8,7,8,15 tell a bleak recent story, and the headgear (t) has not reversed the decline; at OR 86 and with the weakest recent form string in the field, the style compromise compounds what is already a difficult profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a string of eighth-place finishes doing little to inspire confidence, Oneforthegutter does at least return within a month and has run over today's trip and going before — though his rating of 94 suggests more ability than recent efforts have shown.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer at OR 84 whose map position in midfield reflects the overcrowded early sections rather than genuine style — Browne McMonagle is an excellent booking, and three top-four finishes in the last five outings on Good suggest ability, but racing out of position over 2m is a real hurdle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a ninth last time out and his best recent effort a third four starts back, Pole Star has experience over today's distance and going but must bounce back sharply off 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Hermetic
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent type with a thin form line (only three qualifying runs in hist) and an OR of 81; Lemaire is a world-class jockey who can manufacture positions, but the horse must also sit off its natural pace because of field size, and the limited data on Good ground makes assessment difficult.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Hermetic has been largely treading water in recent starts — four finishes outside the placings in his last four, though a winner five starts back shows ability. Has run over today's trip and returns after 42 days off.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner in the field at OR 101 with headgear (ht) and the most weight (143lbs); two wins among the last 15 similar-going runs and placed on Good over 1m4f and 1m6f — the stamina for 2m and the weight burden are the genuine questions, but class superiority cannot be dismissed.
runners_data.comment: Beylerbeyi shaped with plenty of promise when third and second in recent starts, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a serious threat off 143 lb; the concern is he has been winless in his last six starts.

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Mixer is the confirmed front-runner here and, with just one genuine pace-setter in an 11-runner field over 2 miles on Good to Firm ground at Ascot, the tempo will almost certainly be controlled and sustainable rather than pressured. Shrimp Shady and Kilmeaden will press for early positions behind Spirit Mixer, creating a compact prominent group through the long back straight, but nobody will be forcing a truly searching gallop. This plays into the hands of horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and quicken from 3 furlongs out — the Ascot straight rewards those who conserve energy through the middle stages and hit the rising ground with something left. Several runners tagged as hold-up types — Marnier, Oneforthegutter and Pole Star — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more prominent and hold-up horses than can realistically get their natural position, with Shrimp Shady and Mountain Road most likely to secure the prominent berths behind Spirit Mixer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Mixer sets a steady, uncontested gallop and prominent horses travel smoothly into the straight.
scenarios.body: Spirit Mixer dictates at a comfortable clip, allowing Shrimp Shady and Mountain Road to sit close and attack from 3f out without having burned fuel fighting for position; the Ascot straight rewards those who struck the front early in the home turn. Prominent types with strong Good to Firm form get full value from the race shape here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is marginally more honest than expected, stringing the field out and leaving the prominent runners exposed in the straight.
scenarios.body: A genuine gallop over 2 miles on quick ground can catch prominent types flat-footed in the final 2f, opening a gap for true hold-up horses to emerge late from midfield. Beylerbeyi, with the highest OR in the field and proven form over this trip, is best placed to capitalise, while Lavender Hill Mob's record on soft-ish ground is a mild concern here but the horse has placed on Good.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Mixer is allowed to bowl along at its own pace and the field fails to mount a coordinated challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: Over 2 miles on Good to Firm, a relaxed front-runner who conserves energy through the middle stages can prove very hard to reel in if the opposition misjudges the chase in the last half-mile. Spirit Mixer's class-appropriate OR of 94 and recent placed form at this trip suggest a front-running win is a live option if Shrimp Shady and others lack the finishing kick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Squeeze Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops with a bunched midfield and jockeys on redistributed hold-up types manufacture a clear run from 4f out.
scenarios.body: Pole Star or Hermetic, though their natural prominent style is suppressed by the crowded early positions, might find daylight through the wide part of the track if the pace suddenly lifts turning in. The low STYLE_FIT scores and the redistribution of both horses make this an unlikely outcome, but the Ascot straight's width gives them a theoretical path.

watchPoints.text: Shrimp Shady has won three of its last six including twice at 1m6f on Good — if Ryan Moore settles it smoothly in second or third off Spirit Mixer's steady pace, it enters the straight with every advantage.
Beylerbeyi carries 143lbs, 7lbs more than the next-heaviest, and while OR 101 is the class benchmark, watch whether the weight tells in the final furlong of a 2-mile finish on fast ground.
Mountain Road's 69-day absence is the longest in the field — if the horse needs the run or is ring-rusty, Yutaka Take may find it unresponsive when asked to quicken at the top of the straight.

Pole Star, Hermetic and Marnier are all likely to be denied their preferred positions early — watch whether Browne McMonagle on Pole Star attempts to push forward to reclaim a prominent berth, which could disrupt the settled order around the first bend.

Ian Williams saddles three runners (Dancing In Paris, Oneforthegutter, Hermetic) — watch for any stable market moves that indicate which of the three the yard is most confident in, as the stable's 6-from-41 14-day strike rate is respectable and insider intent may be relevant.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Challenge (Class 2 Handicap) (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Claymore
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here; Jane Chapple-Hyam's seven-year-old has strong recent form over 12f on Good ground (winning at this trip in June) and Jerry Chau can dictate uncontested terms, though his STYLE_FIT flag as a P-type rather than natural leader marginally tempers the strength of the lead scenario.
runners_data.comment: Claymore won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat off 142 lb; the worry is that he has been out of the frame in four of his other five recent starts.

runners_data.name: Insanity
runners_data.note: Alan King's six-year-old hold-up performer has placed twice over 10f on Good ground and once at 12f, and Mme Marie Velon's tactical awareness may see her positioned more prominently than habit suggests; 50 days off is the main query, but form and going suit.
runners_data.comment: Insanity has placed twice in his last five starts — second two runs back and second four runs back — and has run over today's trip and going; the concern is a 50-day absence and being yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Frances Ethel
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained mare returning from a 248-day absence, which is the dominant concern here; her best form has come over 10f on Tapeta/Standard, and this 12f Good to Firm assignment looks a significant ask on comeback, making her one to treat with caution.
runners_data.comment: Frances Ethel showed a flash of form with a second last time out, but that came 248 days ago and a return from such a lengthy absence is the key question; winless in her last four starts and carrying 140 lb, she'll need to find improvement.

runners_data.name: Night Breeze
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' consistent six-year-old has three placings in his last four over 10-12f on Good ground including a 12f win, and Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking is a significant positive; the tongue tie is flagged and 11 days since last run is tight, but the profile is among the most compelling in the race.
runners_data.comment: Night Breeze has placed in three of his last four starts, including a win four starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going; however, carrying 140 lb tests his stamina, and with our rating matching his official mark of 97, he lacks a clear edge over the top-rated runners.

runners_data.name: Enemy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with headgear (tp) who won over 16f on Standard but has posted a string of poor efforts on Good ground at shorter trips; Ian Williams runs him, and while the going flag is OK, his recent Good-ground figures are consistently poor and the drop back from 16f is a positive, not a guarantee.
runners_data.comment: Enemy arrives here with experience of both today's trip and going, and his win five starts back shows he can deliver on a similar surface; at 138 lb, the weight is the key question against him.

runners_data.name: Asgard's Captain
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Dylan Cunha on this six-year-old who won over 12f on Good ground two starts ago; his true racing style is hold-up, pushed into a midfield map position because of congestion at the rear, which means Moore may find him fighting for space rather than settled — the style displacement is a real tactical risk.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last two starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Asgard's Captain is hard to fancy at the weights, though he has run over today's distance and going before, and a win four starts back shows he can find the net.

runners_data.name: Castle Stuart
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey's four-year-old has twice placed over 10f on Good ground and holds strong short-trip form, but his natural instinct to race from the rear has been remapped to midfield on this occasion due to the volume of closers in the field; his best efforts over 10f suggest 12f may stretch him.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, Castle Stuart at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a run 28 days ago leaves him fit enough — but a stiff 134 lb and a trainer firing at just 2% recently make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Sportingsilvermine
runners_data.note: James Owen's five-year-old has won twice over 10-12f on Good ground and is a genuine prominent type who should press Claymore; Yutaka Take's bold-riding style could push the front pair on, and if he applies pressure to Claymore he becomes a key pace-shape influencer regardless of his own winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and carrying 134 lb, Sportingsilvermine arrives on the back of an unplaced effort, though a winner two starts back offers a flicker of hope; he has distance and going experience to call on, but it's hard to make a strong case here.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Believer
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's nine-year-old has limited recent Good-ground form and has failed to make the frame in five of his last six runs; a true hold-up performer whose style has been displaced to midfield in the map due to the crowded back end of the field, leaving Saffie Osborne with a positioning puzzle from the off.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, Fantasy Believer does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a trainer firing at 28% in the last fortnight is a clear positive; 132 lb, however, is a stiff ask for a gelding yet to find the winner's enclosure recently.

runners_data.name: Stem
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old has a win over 10f on Good ground and comes here stepping up significantly in trip to 12f; as a prominent-type with genuine early speed he could push Claymore on, but his experience over this distance is very limited and his stamina at this level is an open question.
runners_data.comment: Stem bounced back to winning form last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a clear standout on ratings here. Carrying 132 lb is the one thing to watch, but he arrives fresh at 35 days and looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Genealogy
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's four-year-old has strong form over 16f on Good ground (winning and placing) and wears a tongue tie; racing at 12f looks a trip short of optimum, though the Good to Firm ground suits; his redistribution from rear to midfield on the map means he will need a cleaner passage than his natural style affords.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a string of unplaced efforts, Genealogy is hard to fancy against stronger rivals here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 27 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but his recent form makes a big ask at 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Parlando
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' seven-year-old has a win over 10f on Good ground and comes here without a jockey named, which is immediately notable; a hold-up horse repositioned to midfield in the map, his recent placings have come over shorter trips and his form at 12f in larger fields is modest.
runners_data.comment: Parlando won last time out but that single success masks five largely disappointing efforts in his last six starts, and ranked eleventh of twelve on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going, and 14 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Claymore is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field at 1m4f on Good to Firm ground at Ascot, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jerry Chau can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits, controlling the race from the front rail. Sportingsilvermine and Stem are the only other prominent-profile runners, meaning Claymore is unlikely to be pressured through the early or middle stages, creating a sustainable, uncontested gallop. The bulk of the field — Insanity, Night Breeze, Enemy, Frances Ethel and several redistributed hold-up types — will be tracking from midfield to rear, meaning the closers face a straightforward if congested journey and will need the pace to lift significantly in the straight to reel in any front-runner with daylight. This race shape strongly favours horses with natural tactical speed that can travel prominently or within a few lengths of Claymore, as a steady-to-moderate pace on a flat course will compress the field into the straight and reward those with a turn of foot at the top of the home straight rather than pure stayers grinding from the rear. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Castle Stuart, Asgard's Captain, Fantasy Believer, Genealogy, and Parlando are all true hold-up horses repositioned in midfield on the map, with Night Breeze and Insanity the most likely to actually secure prominent berths among the hold-up brigade based on recent form and jockey profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Claymore Controls, Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Claymore leads unchallenged at a comfortable pace and the closers cannot generate sufficient momentum from the straight.
scenarios.body: Chau sets a relaxed gallop, the field strings out through the final three furlongs, and horses unable to quicken from a slow pace are caught flat-footed; Claymore, racing over a trip that suits his 12f form profile, gets first run and holds on as the closers fail to close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just honest enough for Night Breeze or Insanity to track Claymore and produce a winning burst from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A steady but not dawdling gallop allows the lead to be pegged back in the final two furlongs by a horse that has travelled fluidly in second or third; Night Breeze's consistent 12f form and Dylan Browne McMonagle's positive riding style make this a viable counter-shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently from halfway to stretch the field and allow genuine hold-up horses to finish through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected middle section, perhaps forced by Sportingsilvermine or Stem pushing Claymore, opens ground for the hold-up runners; Genealogy's strong 16f form on good ground and Asgard's Captain's recent 12f win give them the profile to benefit, though their redistribution away from natural positions dampens confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so slow that the entire field converges entering the straight and the race becomes a sprint finish for all 12.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run contest turns the straight into a cavalry charge where tactical luck and draw position matter more than ability; Frances Ethel's recent layoff (248 days) makes her an unlikely beneficiary, but Enemy or Fantasy Believer could get a fortuitous run through, though this scenario is the least likely given Claymore's natural desire to roll along in front.

watchPoints.text: Sportingsilvermine and Stem both have the speed and profile to push Claymore mid-race — watch whether either applies pressure to the leader through the first mile, as this would fundamentally alter whether Claymore's controlled pace advantage holds.

Ryan Moore's booking on Asgard's Captain is significant but watch the first furlong — if he cannot slot comfortably into a natural hold-up position due to field congestion, Moore may burn early energy establishing position and compromise the horse's chance.

Night Breeze ran just 11 days ago and wears a tongue tie; watch his behaviour in the stalls and his jumping action early, as any signs of freshness or sore post-race effects could undermine Dylan Browne McMonagle's ability to deploy him as intended.

Frances Ethel's 248-day absence means she is almost certainly in need of the run from a fitness standpoint — watch how C Y Ho deploys her early to gauge whether William Haggas has her close enough to fitness to be a genuine factor or simply a race-fit builder.

With five or six horses genuinely jostling for the same midfield-to-rear positions, watch the first two furlongs for traffic congestion that could see Castle Stuart, Fantasy Believer, Genealogy and Parlando all compromised before the race has properly developed.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint (Class 2 Handicap)

runners_data.name: Havana Hurricane
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Eve Johnson Houghton who has posted two placed efforts in similar Good ground at 6f recently; sits rearward by style and will need the pace to be genuine to peg back a potentially uncontested leader, with a stat of 10/11 comparable-going runs showing consistency rather than brilliance.
runners_data.comment: Havana Hurricane has run over today's trip and going, arrives on a 28-day break in good order, and our rating puts him top-rated in this field, if only just — a strong threat. The risk is that he's winless in his last five starts, with a ninth last time out suggesting he needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Shaatir
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, Archie Watson's gelding won over this course and trip in Good ground and returns after 116 days with a hood; uncontested lead is the whole shape of this race and if he controls fractions he becomes very hard to pass.
runners_data.comment: Tailed off after a win four starts back, Shaatir has since managed only two fourths and an unplaced effort in recent starts, and a 116-day absence does him no favours; he has run over today's trip and going, but ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, he is hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: May Angel
runners_data.note: Gosden-trained hold-up filly fitted with a tongue-tie who has placed twice in Good-to-Firm conditions but all her best form is over 7f — dropping to 6f on fast ground at Ascot is a non-trivial concern, and Lemaire's booking is the main positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back thirds two and three starts back show May Angel can hit the frame, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is a pair of eighths since then suggest he needs to rediscover that form quickly.

runners_data.name: Red Spells Danger
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne partners a filly who has won twice and placed multiple times on Good ground at 6f, showing the most consistent prominent profile in the field; Tim Easterby's yard is running at a modest 3/82 T14 strike rate but the form string 1-1-2-4-5 gives her the strongest recent credentials of the prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Showed a second three starts back and back-to-back wins in earlier recent starts, but back-to-back fifths and fourths since suggest he's in a dip; a trainer firing at just 4% lately adds caution, though he has distance-and-going experience and a rating of 100 gives him claims.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's 3yo has form figures of 4-6-4-6-7 in her last five which do not inspire, and while she sits prominent by style the trainer's T14 rate of 1/6 is lukewarm; her best form has been at 6f on Good but she has not translated it into a win since May.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Figjam nonetheless has the profile to go well here — she has run over today's trip and going, is fresh on 29 days' absence, and our rating of 106 suggests she's significantly better than her official mark of 92 implies.

runners_data.name: American Gulf
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's gelding missed 310 days between runs and returns off a long break — his two wins include a 6f Good ground success but that layoff is a significant flag and must be factored against his otherwise respectable prominent profile.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed efforts sit on his CV — a winner five starts back and runner-up on each of his last two outings — but 310 days off the track is a significant fitness query, and 137 lb from stall 12 adds further pressure on his return.

runners_data.name: Jel Pepper
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's headgear-wearing (hood) prominent type won over 7f on Good ground last time but his form over 6f shows four placings without a win at the distance; the drop back to a sharp Ascot 6f is a question rather than a certainty, though the Williams yard is firing at 4/34 T14.
runners_data.comment: Jel Pepper has experience over today's distance and going, and a rating of 104 suggests he's significantly better than his official mark of 92 — a potent edge in this field; the worry is he hasn't won in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Cape Ashizuri
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle rides a colt who has won twice at 6f on Good ground and whose most recent run produced a 19th — a poor comeback — but prior form shows a 1-2 sequence at this trip; the 56-day absence is noted but the jockey booking is a significant positive and he is a genuine hold-up horse with strong course-distance credentials.
runners_data.comment: Cape Ashizuri won two starts back and has run over today's trip, but he comes here on the back of an unplaced effort and a 56-day absence, so fitness is the key question under 136 lb from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Thunder Call
runners_data.note: William Haggas has this horse in the best form of his life — three runs showing 1-1-2 — and the yard's 10/52 T14 rate is the strongest in the race; prominent by style and suited by Good to Firm, he is the most in-form runner arriving at this race.
runners_data.comment: Thunder Call won two of his last five starts and returns in solid nick after 30 days, with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour; however, he was third last time out and his ranking of seventh suggests he faces stiffer competition here.

runners_data.name: Grasmere Boy
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's colt has won his last two starts and clearly has ability, but he is a natural front-end/prominent racer who cannot secure his preferred berth in a field this congested — his chance hinges on finding a cleaner run than his mapped position allows, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 should temper expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Beaten fifth last time out despite back-to-back wins before that, Grasmere Boy arrives at a below-par speed rating of 75 and ranks tenth of twelve on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going, and the 14-day turnaround is fine, but he's hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Anyasi
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's unexposed filly is unbeaten in two starts including a 6f Good ground win, making her an intriguing entry, but she too is a prominent type who will struggle to get her natural position here; her limited race experience at three starts is an additional unknown in a 12-runner competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and carrying a hefty 135 lb, Anyasi is hard to fancy despite winning two of his last three starts — a winner last time and again two starts back — with experience over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 34% in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's hold-up sprinter has won twice over 5f on Good ground and all five historical runs are at 5f — stepping up to 6f at Ascot is an unproven trip, and while he is a genuine hold-up type the trip question means he is harder to assess than his recent wins suggest.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our assessments, One And Gone is hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins two and three starts back; he was unplaced last time out and rates a tough ask against stronger rivals here, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Shaatir is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, should stride clear from the gates and set a sustainable, unforced gallop on this Good to Firm Ascot 6f. Behind him, Red Spells Danger, Figjam, American Gulf, Jel Pepper, and Thunder Call all want prominent positions, creating a congested group of five chasing the leader — traffic and checking risks are real between the 2f and 3f poles as that group compresses. The hold-up horses Havana Hurricane, May Angel, Cape Ashizuri, and One And Gone will be tracking or rearward of this scrum and will need the pace to be genuinely strong enough to set up a closing run, which is not guaranteed with only one horse forcing it. This race shape most favours a single prominent racer who slots in behind Shaatir smoothly and travels into the race without burning energy in the early scrimmage — the risk for deep closers is that Shaatir's uncontested lead allows him to control fractions and the pace may not be truly searching enough to pull them through. This field holds more prominent types than can all secure their ideal position: Red Spells Danger, with her consistent form and course record, and Thunder Call are best placed by draw, jockey quality, and recent form to actually claim the prime slots behind the leader; Grasmere Boy and Anyasi, both true prominent racers redistributed to midfield in this map, are the ones most likely to find themselves racing out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shaatir Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Shaatir leads uncontested at a fair pace and one prominent racer slots cleanly into the slipstream to pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Shaatir dictates fractions from the front, the prominent group sorts itself out by halfway, and the horse travelling smoothest in second or third sweeps past in the final 100 yards; Good to Firm rewards a clean, prominent-to-lead run without the need for a deep finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front-Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion behind Shaatir produces checking and scrubbing along, leaving him alone in front to steal the race on a falsely-run fractions.
scenarios.body: The early scrimmage between five prominent types disrupts their rhythm and frees Shaatir to bowl along unchallenged; his two wins over this course and distance configuration give him the tactical profile to sustain a lead when not pressured.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Shaatir's fractions are genuinely brisk enough and the prominent traffic jam stalls the chasing group, opening a clear late lane for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Cape Ashizuri and Havana Hurricane are the truest hold-up types with the form to close late on fast ground, and a strung-out field after early chaos could leave the rail or outer clear for a finishing run; note however that the single front-runner makes a truly strong gallop less certain, which limits this scenario's likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Grasmere Boy or Anyasi, both natural prominent types forced wider in the early stages, find a smooth passage and arrive late from an unfavourable map position.
scenarios.body: Because both horses are racing out of their natural role their chance is materially discounted — but Grasmere Boy's back-to-back wins and Anyasi's unbeaten record at this trip give them raw ability to overcome a positional disadvantage if circumstances unfold messily.

watchPoints.text: Shaatir breaks cleanly — if he misses the break even marginally, the prominent quintet could swallow him and the entire race shape collapses; watch his exit from the stalls as the first critical moment.

The five prominent runners (Red Spells Danger, Figjam, American Gulf, Jel Pepper, Thunder Call) will contest positions 2-6 in the opening furlong — crowding and bumping between the 5f and 4f poles is a live risk that could unbalance any of them.

Cape Ashizuri's homework run of 19th last time is an obvious concern — if that was a prep rather than a true form line, Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking suggests connections expect a bounce-back, but punters should watch his early behaviour and position.

American Gulf has been off 310 days — horses returning from that length of absence at Ascot in a competitive handicap often need the run, and his early positioning and how he travels after halfway will tell you quickly whether the layoff is a concern.

One And Gone has run all five career starts over 5f — watch whether he is travelling fluently at halfway, as this is his first test at 6f and any sign of him shortening his stride at the 3f pole would confirm the trip is beyond him today.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic (Class 3 Handicap) (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Archers Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two wins at around 1m2f on good ground and Ryan Moore booked — a serious contender to lead, though stepping back up to 1m4f after a finishing fourth last time asks a question of his stamina under 142lbs.
runners_data.comment: Archers Bay shaped well with a third three starts back and has winning form in his recent starts, giving him solid claims stepping up here; the main worry is his fourth last time out suggests he may not always fire on demand.

runners_data.name: Hoseki
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old filly arrives on a hat-trick of wins, all at 1m2f-1m4f on good or similar ground, and Saffie Osborne maintains the partnership; the form profile is the strongest in the race at face value.
runners_data.comment: Hoseki arrives in cracking form, winning three of her last five starts, and has run over today's trip and going before. Carrying 138 lb is the one query, but three recent victories speak for themselves.

runners_data.name: Baltic Fleet
runners_data.note: Prominent-running type with a visor fitted, returning quickly after just 10 days — has placed at 1m4f-1m5f but yet to win over this trip, and Jerry Chau's inexperience at Ascot is a minor question mark.
runners_data.comment: Baltic Fleet shaped with plenty of promise when second and third in recent starts, and his win from five runs back underlines he knows how to find the line; he has run over today's trip and, at 136 lb, the weight is the one obvious concern after his pulled-up effort last time.

runners_data.name: Blue Hercules
runners_data.note: Jamie Melham rides this William Muir-trained colt who has placed twice at 1m4f on good ground but cannot quite get his head in front; the honest pace here suits his prominent style and he warrants respect each-way.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last five starts — second last time out and a second three starts back — Blue Hercules arrives fit enough on 28 days' rest with experience over today's trip and going, but he's winless in recent starts and his ranking of seventh of 11 suggests he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Pierre Grosse
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's consistent hold-up performer has been placed on seven of eight runs on good ground and twice at 1m4f — Ferraris rides and the horse should love the conditions, though he needs a strong pace to produce his best.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Pierre Grosse has run over today's trip and going and arrives here fit on a 20-day turnaround carrying 135 lb — a strong each-way profile; the risk is he remains winless in his last five despite that persistent proximity.

runners_data.name: Royal Poetry
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's colt has won over 1m4f on good ground and placed several times at the trip; Yutaka Take is a notable Shergar Cup booking and the horse's consistent form over this distance makes him a live each-way option.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in her last six starts with a second last time out, Royal Poetry brings solid recent form and distance-and-going experience; however, carrying 130 lb against stronger-rated rivals makes life harder for her here.

runners_data.name: King Of Berkshire
runners_data.note: Lemaire partners this Andrew Balding front-runner who has won twice on good ground at up to 1m4f — likely to go with Archers Bay for the lead from the off; will need to be stronger than his OR=79 suggests to last home if pressed.
runners_data.comment: King Of Berkshire showed a win three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but his last two outings — fourth and third — suggest he's finding the top level tough, and 129 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Level Look
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly returns quickly (6 days) but has won over 1m2f on soft/standard and her best form has come on more testing surfaces; Mme Valle Skar rides in the Shergar Cup context and she may find Good to Firm quicker than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Level Look is hard to fancy at these weights despite a win three starts back and an encouraging second last time out; he has run over today's trip and going, but his speed rating of 75 leaves him with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Ohara
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's colt was a 15th last time at 1m4f on good ground which raises a flag, though his previous run was second over the same trip — Dylan Browne McMonagle is a strong jockey booking but the recent form needs to be forgiven to trust him here.
runners_data.comment: Showed a second two starts back but has been unplaced most recently, and that eighth and ninth in between are a concern; has run over today's trip and going, and 14 days is a fair enough gap, though he'll need to find improvement on recent efforts at 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Last Verse
runners_data.note: Joseph Parr's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who has form at 1m4f including a win over 1m2f; with several hold-up types in this field, Narredu may find him shuffled back further than ideal — his best chance depends on a strong, true gallop burning out the leaders.
runners_data.comment: Last Verse shaped well for third last time out, and a winner two starts back, but he ranks ninth of eleven on our figures and that gap to the principals is hard to overlook despite his experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Tai Hang Pegasus
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes's colt is a natural prominent-racing type who has won and placed at 1m4f on good ground — with the prominent berths already occupied by stronger rivals, he is likely to find himself covering more ground than his style demands, tempering confidence at current odds.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and returning just two days after his last outing, Tai Hang Pegasus faces a stiff ask, though he has experience of today's trip and going and won last time out.

races.paceDynamic: Archers Bay and King Of Berkshire are the two confirmed front-runners in this 11-runner 1m4f handicap on Good to Firm ground, and with both likely to push for the lead from the off, this race will be run at an honest, competitive gallop from the start — there will be no crawl and no false pace. Archers Bay, trained by Marco Botti and ridden by Ryan Moore, has won twice at around this trip and will not surrender the lead cheaply; King Of Berkshire, handled by Lemaire for Andrew Balding, has form at 1m4f on good ground and will press hard. The sustained pace they create plays into the hands of horses who can sit prominently or in mid-division and pick up into the straight once the fractions take their toll on the leaders. The field also contains more prominent-running types than can realistically secure that position — Baltic Fleet, Blue Hercules, Hoseki and Royal Poetry all want to race close to the pace, meaning Tai Hang Pegasus (a natural prominent type) and Last Verse (a genuine hold-up horse) are likely to find themselves further back than ideal. This race shape — an honest gallop with a contested lead — strongly favours horses who can race prominently in second or third without burning petrol early and sustain their effort into the Ascot straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Archers Bay and King Of Berkshire fight for the lead at a genuine clip, setting it up for horses sitting just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The honest early gallop burns out both leaders approaching the straight, leaving the horses who tracked them — Hoseki, Blue Hercules, Royal Poetry — best placed to pounce; on Good to Firm ground at Ascot the prominent hold is gold, and Hoseki's hat-trick form over this trip gives her strong claims.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Brave It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong but one of the front-runners, specifically Archers Bay, proves classier than the rating and sustains the effort.
scenarios.body: Archers Bay's two recent wins over similar trips and Ryan Moore's handling of a strong gallop could see him dictate and simply not come back to the field; King Of Berkshire fades having been outpaced for the lead, and the finish resolves itself early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Sweeper Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is intense enough to flatten all prominent types, allowing a horse held up in midfield to pick up late through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: Pierre Grosse, who has been placed at 1m4f and 1m5f on good ground repeatedly, could thread through from midfield if the leaders empty quickly; Level Look showed stamina winning over 1m2f at the last run and carries a light weight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Flat, Hold-Up Undoes
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses mid-race and horses like Last Verse or Tai Hang Pegasus, racing out of their natural role, fail to travel smoothly enough to land a blow.
scenarios.body: Both Last Verse and Tai Hang Pegasus carry a style-fit discount having been pushed back from their natural positions, and a messy tactical race with a stop-start tempo leaves them with no clear run from the rear; the race devolves into a sprint from 2f out that favours the fastest-finishing prominent types.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a battle between Archers Bay and King Of Berkshire from the first furlong — if both refuse to yield, the pace could be strong enough to set up the race for Hoseki and the prominent stalkers rather than either leader.
Baltic Fleet is fitted with a visor and returns after only 10 days — watch his keenness in the early stages; if he over-races behind the two leaders he may not get home at 1m4f.

Tai Hang Pegasus was last seen just two days ago and is a natural prominent type who may struggle to get his position in a field stacked with pace — watch his position at the start to judge whether he can hold a forward slot or is immediately shuffled back.

Pierre Grosse has been second twice in his last three runs and goes well fresh on good ground — if the leaders set a true pace and begin to tire entering the straight, watch for him to make smooth late progress from the rear of the prominent group.

Royal Poetry's jockey Yutaka Take rides in the Shergar Cup and may adopt an aggressive position early to maximise the trip — watch how far up he settles in the first two furlongs as that will determine whether Royal Poetry is a genuine threat or an also-ran.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile (Class 2 Handicap)

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner; David O'Meara's five-year-old has strong recent course form and a 13/15 record on similar going, will lead from the front on Good to Firm at Ascot, though OR=106 means rivals are well-handicapped to peg it back.|
runners_data.comment: Cerulean Bay finished second last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while an official mark of 106 suggests he retains plenty of ability — the concern is that he's winless in his last six starts, which may hint at a finishing-line issue.

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride on Richard Spencer's horse, whose recent form has been over 6-7f — the step up to a mile is a key query, but has run well on similar going and will seek to track the leader throughout.|
runners_data.comment: Ran second two starts back and returns here just seven days later, fresh and fit; Two Tribes has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 113 ranks him second among these twelve. The worry is he's winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Crown Board
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for Jane Chapple-Hyam and amateur rider Mme Frida Valle Skar; placed twice in eight recent outings at this trip on good ground, will need a stronger pace than anticipated to deliver her finish from the back.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent at the top of the weights, Crown Board has been placed in two of his last three starts and steps back out just 14 days on, bringing experience of today's trip and conditions. Winless in recent starts, but the form profile makes him the one to beat from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Mister Winston
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old won over this course and distance on good ground and has three wins on similar surfaces; prominent racer who should get a natural position in this shape — the booking of Jerry Chau fits the Shergar Cup team context.|
runners_data.comment: Mister Winston has shown he can win, with victories three and five starts back, but consecutive unplaced runs since make him hard to fancy, and our figures rank him near the foot of the field. Has run over today's trip and going, and eight days fresh.

runners_data.name: Ebt's Guard
runners_data.note: William Muir & Chris Grassick's five-year-old has multiple placed efforts at this trip on good ground; a confirmed prominent type who should slot into the chasing group naturally, though his form string shows no win in six recent attempts.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though a third two runs back shows there's ability lurking; has run over today's trip and going, and comes back quickly on eight days' rest, but that ninth last time out is harder to ignore from stall seven off 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Fondo Blanco
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old sports a tongue-tie and returns after 51 days off; most of her wins came on soft ground (1W on soft/8f) so the Good to Firm conditions here represent a genuine concern, though she will race prominently.|
runners_data.comment: Fondo Blanco showed he can win at this level, scoring two starts back, but an unplaced effort last time out and 51 days off the track raise freshness questions; experience over today's trip and going is a plus, though his mark of 102 gives rivals a look-in.

runners_data.name: Bullet Point
runners_data.note: William Haggas's five-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose 84-day absence is noted; wears a hood and returns from a lengthy break — his instinct to race forward will likely be frustrated by the crowded prominent group, placing him in midfield against his will.|
runners_data.comment: Bullet Point landed a win five starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, while his rating of 109 suggests he holds plenty of ability — the concern is a 84-day absence and a run of unplaced efforts in his last four starts since.

runners_data.name: Popmaster
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's eight-year-old wants to race close to the pace but finds himself one of several prominent types unable to claim that position; limited recent form on good going (4/15 runs on sim going without a win), and this compromised role undermines an already modest chance.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Popmaster nevertheless brings distance and going experience to the table and comes from a yard firing at 28% in the last fortnight; 35 days between runs and 132 lb from stall six are the checks against him here.

runners_data.name: Ozat
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount on Ian Williams's five-year-old, who has a modest record on good ground (6/15 sim-going) and a poor recent form string; a hold-up horse who needs strong pace to produce his best — Moore's quality is the main hook.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and unplaced in four of them, Ozat faces a stiff task from stall 8 carrying 132 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 104 offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Serengeti
runners_data.note: Mike Murphy's four-year-old drops back in trip having won over 10f on good ground; his trainer's 14-day record is 0/6 and he has been off 50 days — a hold-up type who could benefit if the pace genuinely heats up, but the trip and layoff are risks.|
runners_data.comment: Serengeti has been unplaced in three of his last six starts, with only a single win to show in that recent stretch, and he ranks tenth of twelve on our figures. Has run over today's distance and going, and that sole win two starts back offers slim hope.

runners_data.name: Storm Star
runners_data.note: A true prominent racer for Andrew Balding, but with multiple prominent types in the field he is unlikely to get his preferred position; 51 days off, limited wins on good ground (0W from sim-going runs), and the compromised mapping makes this a difficult assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Storm Star is hard to fancy, though a return from 51 days off and experience over today's trip and going offer slim grounds for optimism.

runners_data.name: Hickory
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's eight-year-old is another genuine prominent type who will struggle to land a forward berth; wears a hood, has a solid record on similar going (12/15) with two wins at this trip, but age and the overcrowded prominent group work against him running to his best.|
runners_data.comment: Hickory won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but that single win in his last five starts and a ranking of 12th in the field on our figures make him hard to fancy, despite the 14-day turnaround leaving him fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Cerulean Bay is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Ascot over a mile, is likely to stride into a clear lead from the outset and control a steady, metronomic tempo without any meaningful pressure from rivals. Two Tribes, Mister Winston, Ebt's Guard and Fondo Blanco are all prominent types who will contest the positions just behind the leader, but none has the pure gate speed or role to challenge Cerulean Bay for the front. The field holds more genuinely prominent and front-running types than the race shape can accommodate — Bullet Point, Popmaster, Storm Star and Hickory are all true prominent racers who are likely to be pushed back into midfield against their natural inclinations, compromising their ability to produce their best form. With a single uncontested pace-setter operating on fast ground at a circuit that punishes those who wait too long, this race shape strongly favours horses with a prominent or close-tracking running style who can sit in Cerulean Bay's slipstream and kick off a true pace — hold-up horses face a stern test if the tempo is not strong enough to bring them into play in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cerulean Bay Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Cerulean Bay settles into an uncontested lead and the prominent chasers cannot summon a devastating turn of foot.
scenarios.body: Cerulean Bay dictates a controlled pace and the proximity horses who track it — Mister Winston, Two Tribes and Ebt's Guard — get the perfect racing position to pounce approaching the furlong pole; on Good to Firm ground the advantage of sitting close to the pace throughout is maximised.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chasers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of prominent types settle just off Cerulean Bay and one of them produces a decisive kick turning in.
scenarios.body: Two Tribes or Ebt's Guard sits close to the pace in the prime tracking position and fires past a tiring Cerulean Bay inside the final furlong, with the others strung out behind; this scenario rewards those who naturally race just off the lead and are not forced to reroute their running style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If Cerulean Bay sets a genuinely strong gallop that stretches the field and creates a true end-to-end test.
scenarios.body: Crown Board and Serengeti, genuine hold-up horses, are able to come through on the outside once the pace-setters crack in the final two furlongs; this scenario requires a faster-than-expected tempo to materialise and is less likely given Cerulean Bay's tendency to find a rhythm rather than burn along.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Bounce Back
scenarios.trigger: If several prominent horses pushed back in the map manage to work forward early and disrupt the anticipated race shape.
scenarios.body: Bullet Point, Storm Star or Popmaster, all true prominent racers who may drift forward from their mapped midfield positions, could yet find a spot closer to the pace than expected and produce their best form; however, all carry a style-fit discount given the overcrowded prominent group and the difficulty of overcoming a compromised position in a race this steady.

watchPoints.text: Cerulean Bay — if it secures a clean, uncontested lead and the pace is pedestrian, the race could be over a long way from home before hold-up horses can respond.

Bullet Point, Storm Star, Popmaster and Hickory — all natural prominent types likely to be shuffled back against their instincts; watch for early scrimmaging for position in the first two furlongs that could unsettle any of them.
Fondo Blanco — the step to Good to Firm is a significant conditions question given all her wins came on soft ground; monitor her movement in the betting as market moves may reflect stable confidence.
Ryan Moore on Ozat — Moore frequently conjures performances beyond a horse's rating; watch for him angling wide to find clear daylight in the closing stages even if his mount's recent form is modest.
Crown Board — the amateur rider (Mme Frida Valle Skar, Shergar Cup) handles a genuine hold-up type that needs everything to go right; any pace collapse will leave her with nothing to aim at.
